trust_decision.summary: Archive bytes from an untrusted zip are fed to an async zlib inflate stream; the library decides whether a decompression failure is reported to the caller's callback or escapes as an unhandled 'error' event (process crash). Decided in methods/inflater.js inflateAsync (no 'error' listener) and in zipEntry.js decompress async branch (callback ignores err).

landing_point.why: Summary says 'unhandled error event in async DEFLATE decompression'; inflateAsync creates the zlib stream with only 'data'/'end' listeners.

fix_sites.entry_point: ZipEntry.getDataAsync (zipEntry.js:309-314) and AdmZip async readers (adm-zip.js:157-160, adm-zip.js:192-195, adm-zip.js:893)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: zipEntry.js:110-118 (decompress callback must propagate the new err instead of CRC-checking the empty placeholder buffer)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The sync-throw routes in async decompress (bad password, unknown method, bad local header, STORED bad CRC) are 'synchronous exceptions documented as throws', not zlib error events, so a solver can argue they are outside an advisory about the DEFLATE stream.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The maxOutputLength cap (fix for CVE-2026-39244) must stay: it is itself a source of stream errors, so a fix that drops the cap to avoid errors reopens the decompression bomb; also valid DEFLATE entries must still decode and bad-CRC entries must still deliver data plus BAD_CRC exactly once.

O6_input_shapes: real output exceeding declared size (maxOutputLength RangeError)
error after partial data / end-after-error (single callback guard)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Encrypted entry with wrong password: ZipCrypto.decrypt throws synchronously inside async decompress; from extractAllToAsync the 2nd+ entry is decompressed inside an fs.utimes callback, so the throw is uncaught.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Password errors are a sync API contract and belong to a neighbouring (encryption) feature.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: STORED entry with bad CRC calls the callback with BAD_CRC and then also throws in async mode (double signal + uncaught throw from async extraction chain).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: STORED is not DEFLATE; the advisory names DEFLATE only.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Unknown compression method calls callback then throws in async mode.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Unsupported method is a legacy/unsupported-combination path.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Malformed local header: getCompressedDataFromZip -> loadLocalHeaderFromBinary throws INVALID_LOC before any async work, uncaught when reached from the extractAllToAsync chain.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Header parsing is a different layer from decompression.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: deflateAsync has the same stream pattern with no 'error' listener (second implementation of the same stream wrapper, used by toBuffer/toBufferPromise via zipFile.js:391).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is a copy-paste twin of inflateAsync; a maintainer fixing inflate would plausibly forget it, though input is in-memory data so a real error is hard to trigger.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An async extract/readFile variant that wraps getDataAsync without try/catch around sync throws.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: extractAllToAsync already chains getDataAsync inside fs callbacks; a per-entry async extractEntryTo would be a natural addition.

O9_family: CWE-248 uncaught exception in async error path (unhandled stream 'error' event) leading to process crash

O10_build.project_tests: test/crc/index.js (async bad-CRC callback), test/decompress_bomb.test.js (sync only), test/methods/methods.test.js (extractAllToAsync)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add tmp.on('error') in inflateAsync that calls callback(buf, err), leaving zipEntry's callback to ignore err and the sync throws in async decompress untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: Crash/DoS class in a small library: lessons-v2 records resource-exhaustion and small-library hosts as never hard; how-type room is limited to the maxOutputLength coupling.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (source is a handful of JS files, clearly < 5 MB).
Whether the advisory text counts sync throws in async decompress (O8) as within its property is inferred from the summary, not the full advisory body.
